description: Codex agentic routing configuration — selects the model for OpenAI-Responses-style requests emitted by the Codex CLI agent, based on the request class (main turn, auxiliary title generation, context compaction) and on the work mode of the turn (planning, implementing, testing, reviewing, debugging).

codex_modes.name: plan
codex_modes.description: The requested action is planning: defining architecture, scope, strategy or a sequence of work before editing files. Selected for Codex Plan Mode and explicit requests for an approach or design. Planning a GitHub integration or a testing strategy remains planning, not Git operations or writing tests; inspection alone is review unless a plan is requested.

codex_modes.name: implement
codex_modes.description: The requested action is creating or editing application code, configuration or documentation. Implementing a GitHub integration is code work, not Git history review; creating a demo mock is implementation, not an automated test. Editing README or CHANGELOG from an already completed analysis is implementation, not reviewing that analysis. Writing tests belongs to test, and diagnosing a concrete code failure belongs to debug. This is the default main-turn mode and fallback when no more specific mode is detected.

codex_modes.name: test
codex_modes.description: The requested action is writing or running automated tests, measuring coverage, or repairing test code, assertions and fixtures. Repairing a test means correcting the test itself; finding the root cause of an application failure exposed by a test belongs to debug. A mock used in an automated test belongs here, while a mock for a demo belongs to implement. Checking README against configuration by reading files is review, not test execution.

codex_modes.name: git_review
codex_modes.description: The requested action concerns Git state or history: inspecting diffs, branches, commits, pull or merge requests, comparing branches, resolving Git conflicts or performing commit, push, pull, rebase, merge, cherry-pick, checkout and worktree operations. Summarizing commits belongs here; editing CHANGELOG from an existing summary belongs to implement. GitHub as the subject of an integration does not make code implementation a Git task. Reviewing current code or documentation without a Git comparison belongs to review.

codex_modes.name: review
codex_modes.description: The requested action is inspecting existing code, configuration or documentation and reporting potential problems or inconsistencies without editing files or diagnosing a concrete failure. Checking README against configuration, including documented model assignments, is a read-only consistency review, not automated test execution. Reviewing Git diffs or commit history belongs to git_review; editing the reviewed files belongs to implement; investigating an observed crash or regression belongs to debug.

codex_modes.name: debug
codex_modes.description: The requested action is diagnosing or repairing a concrete application failure: an exception, crash, hang, incorrect result or regression. A failing test can expose that failure, but the goal here is finding or fixing the underlying code defect, not updating assertions or fixtures. Writing or running tests belongs to test; inspecting code for potential issues without an observed failure belongs to review.
